source.title: Prefrontal and striatal dopaminergic genes predict individual differences in exploration and exploitation

confidence_rationale: Strong, high-quality demonstration that a distinct 'directed exploration' mechanism -- choosing in proportion to Bayesian uncertainty about whether an unknown option beats the status quo -- exists, varies across individuals, and is controlled by a neural/genetic system (prefrontal COMT) dissociable from the striatal system that governs reward exploitation. This directly supports the PLAUSIBILITY half of Q-089: that agents can differ systematically in an uncertainty-resolution/information-seeking parameter that is separable from raw learning ability. It does NOT test the specific Q-089 claim (that such a difference predicts a cold-start competence split among REE seeds better than initialisation/difficulty/premature-death controls). Confidence held at 0.5 because mapping fidelity is moderate and transfer risk (human genetic individual differences -> RL random-seed differences) is high; it evidences the mechanism's reality, not the causal split.
failure_signatures: The dissociation is between individual humans with different genotypes, not between random seeds of one learner; a seed's 'directed-exploration parameter' has no genetic analogue and may be pinned or degenerate.

Directed exploration here is measured on a temporal decision task with explicitly signalled uncertainty; in a sparse REE environment the uncertainty signal driving orient/survey may be absent or unmeasurable, so the parameter that varies in humans may not even be observable across seeds.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A gene primarily controlling prefrontal dopamine function (COMT) is associated with a particular type of 'directed exploration', in which exploratory decisions are made in proportion to Bayesian uncertainty about whether other choices might produce outcomes better than the status quo; striatal genes (DARPP-32, DRD2) instead govern exploitative reward learning. Quantitative model fits show genetic factors modulate independent parameters of a reinforcement-learning system.
mapping.ree_translation: The uncertainty-proportional 'directed exploration' parameter is the biological analogue of REE's MECH-482 epistemic-deficit accumulator and MECH-483 orient/survey regime: a drive to sample in proportion to resolvable uncertainty about whether a better option exists. That this parameter (i) is real, (ii) varies across agents, and (iii) is mechanistically separable from reward-exploitation supports the premise that REE seeds could differ in how strongly/early they enter orient/survey mode independently of their raw competence.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This evidences only that a directed-exploration mechanism EXISTS and varies between agents -- it does not show that such variation drives a competence SPLIT, nor that it out-predicts the initialisation/difficulty/premature-death/curriculum confounds Q-089 must rule out. The between-human-genotype variation is a poor analogue for between-random-seed variation in a single RL substrate.
mapping.source_context: Human adults; temporal (clock) decision-making task with a computational reinforcement-learning model; candidate-gene (COMT, DARPP-32, DRD2) association analysis.

confidence_components.notes: Nature Neuroscience, canonical and heavily cited; robust computational modelling with a genetic double dissociation. Mapping fidelity moderate because it grounds the mechanism's reality but not the Q-089 causal-split test; transfer risk high (human genotype -> RL seed, signalled-uncertainty task -> sparse REE env).
